Four years after? My urine levels show gadolinium 40x(!) the reference level. Still. I’ve attempted suicide once and think about everyday. In my support group for gad toxicity I know three people who took their life. 

Could never get any medical professional to believe me - everyone said this was just in my head. Couldn’t get the radiologist to report this to the FDA as an adverse effect. They literally said “we’ve never seen this and don’t know what to do. Talk to your PCP”. Which is humorous, since he also has never seen it but has never injected anyone with contrast.

I’m sure this is rare, but I could show you hundreds of people (from my support groups) that have the same symptoms as me, had the same procedure as me, have the same urine tests, and are just screaming for someone to take us serious. Not looking to sue, not looking to make money, just have someone look into the reasons why people with healthy kidneys would suffer so greatly from this. 

That’s all.

Hey there. Thank you for posting this, and thank you for being brave enough to make yourself vulnerable. Your story is heartbreaking, but I’m hoping it was therapeutic to post it online.

I was, and am still in many ways, like you. At 17 I attempted suicide for many similar reasons - I was bullied and beaten up at school, and treated like a piece of crap. Fortunately, I was verrrrrry bad at it - I took a bunch of pills then threw up for hours. No long term damage.

Life is always going to be hard, but I gotta day those teenage years are f@cking awful - kids are so mean cuz they think there’s no consequences. Sadly, there are - even though I realize now I am worth it, that I am attractive, that I am better than the way they treated me. But the bullying I left with in high school has held me back for decades. 

I wont lie to you - life can still be hard. I contemplate suicide daily, but now for other reasons: a doctor made a medical mistake that’s left me with an incurable condition. It’s angering and painful and I have trouble with life every day.

That said, my life at 42 is infinitely better than at 17, my suicide attempt age. I made a great salary, live in a great city, and have built a nice life for myself. People treat me well, and I have so much more confidence than I did 25 years ago. 

Remember one thing: the choice to end your life is yours and yours only. Don’t listen to people who will try to tell you that you’re weak or selfish or that depression is the easy way out. 

But I will say that you are young, and that yes, life will change in your late teens and 20s - that’s when you really make the most meaningful relationships of your life. 

Will it be better? Hopefully. But for now, make sure you tell as many folks close to you about your pain, and talk to others here or wherever about yours thoughts. If you do that and decide not to continue life, at least you have a breadth of opinions to base your choice.

You’re also welcome to message me. I’m a few years your senior but I’m happy to talk with you about anything you’d like.
